history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Samosharan Temple is one of the popular Jain temples at Madhuban, the base village of Parasnath Hill (Shri Sammed Shikharji Tirth), the holiest Jain pilgrimage site. It is described by templeyatri.in as dedicated to Lord Mahavira (the 24th Tirthankara), with intricate carvings depicting scenes from his life. UNVERIFIED: local sources (99mustsee) claim a Madhuban temple more than 2000 years old, but the temple's age, patronage and architecture are not reliably documented; ICOMOS notes no ancient religious monuments beyond the 18th century on Parasnath Hill. No dedicated image of this temple was found after targeted searching - media is empty by design. Coordinates are approximate (Madhuban foothill).

name: Samosharan Temple, Madhuban
town: Madhuban (CSV town 'Giridih' is WRONG - the temple is at Madhuban village, Pirtand block)
town_description: Madhuban is the base village of Parasnath Hill in Pirtand block, Giridih district, Jharkhand. It is the gateway to Shri Sammed Shikharji Tirth, where 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras are believed to have attained moksha. The village hosts popular Jain temples such as Samosharan and Bhomiyaji Asthan, and a Jain Museum whose balcony telescope gives a clear sight of the Parasnath temple. Trekking routes of 9-13 km to the hilltop start here; Parasnath railway station is about 25 km away.
